title: Flowchart Drawing Workshop
objectives: Build a flowchart from scratch from a given problem description

hook.text: Now you know the rules. It is your turn: turn a few problems into flowcharts from scratch.

concept.heading: Workshop time
concept.body: This lesson has no new concept. You will combine everything you have learned (symbols, linear flow, pseudocode translation) to build flowcharts from scratch. For each problem, first put the steps in order in your head, then place the right symbol in the right spot.

exercises.question: Build the flowchart for the algorithm "get a name from the user and greet them".
Build the flowchart for the algorithm "multiply two numbers and print the result".
Build the flowchart for the algorithm "calculate the circumference of a circle (CONST PI ← 3.14)".
Which symbol should you place first when building a flowchart?

feedback.correct: Correct. Every flowchart begins with a "Start" terminal.
feedback.incorrect: The first symbol of every flowchart is the "Start" terminal.

exercises.question: Put the thinking order to follow when building a flowchart in the correct order.
steps: Assign the right symbol to each step

exercises.question: Which symbol shows the step "a ← a + 1" in a flowchart?

feedback.correct: Correct. An assignment is always shown with the process (rectangle) symbol.
feedback.incorrect: Assignments (with ←) are shown with the process (rectangle) symbol.

summary: How to build a flowchart: split the problem, put the steps in order, pick the right symbol, connect with arrows.
Each step matches a symbol: READ/WRITE → input/output, assignment → process, IF → decision.
With practice, building flowcharts becomes as natural as writing pseudocode.
